title: Multiplication Facts
subtitle: Factors to 5, up to 15
bounds: PROTOCOL §4c (Facts: number size is the difficulty axis). Prompt a × b = ? with whole numbers, exact. Tier bands by larger factor: T1 both 1-5 (25 prompts); T2 larger 6-8, both 2-8 (33); T3 larger 9-10, both 2-10 (32); T4 larger 11-12, both 2-12 (40); T5 larger 13-15, both 2-15 (75); product at most 225. Wrong choices are distinct non-negative whole numbers up to 999, at least two within the larger factor of the answer (one group off, or the answer plus or minus 10 on tiers 4-5), at most one far; on tiers 4-5 every item holds a wrong value with the answer's ones digit.

tiers.name: Up to 5 × 5
tiers.description: Multiplication facts with both factors from 1 to 5.

tiers.name: Up to 8 × 8
tiers.description: Facts with a factor of 6, 7 or 8. Use doubles and 5s.

tiers.name: Up to 10 × 10
tiers.description: The full times table through 10 × 10, 9s and 10s included.

tiers.name: Up to 12 × 12
tiers.description: Facts with 11 and 12. Split into tens and ones.

tiers.name: Up to 15 × 15
tiers.description: Facts with 13, 14 and 15. Split a factor, then add the parts.

GROUP_OFF.student: One group too many or too few. Count the groups, then the size of each.
GROUP_OFF.teacher: Off by one group: a × (b + 1), a × (b − 1), (a + 1) × b or (a − 1) × b.

ADDED.student: × means equal groups, not +. 4 × 3 is 4 groups of 3, which is 12.
ADDED.teacher: Adds the factors instead of multiplying: 4 × 3 = 7.

DROPPED_CARRY.student: Keep the ten: 13 × 6 is 60 + 18, and the 18 has a ten to add in.
DROPPED_CARRY.teacher: Splits into tens and ones but loses the ten from the ones product: 13 × 6 = 60 + 8 = 68.

TENS_SLIP.student: Check the tens place. Split into tens and ones, multiply each, add both.
TENS_SLIP.teacher: Right ones digit, tens place off by one ten (product plus or minus 10).

PARTIAL_PRODUCTS.student: Tens × tens plus ones × ones skips two parts. Split one number, multiply both.
PARTIAL_PRODUCTS.teacher: Multiplies tens by tens and ones by ones only: 13 × 14 = 100 + 12 = 112.
